entries.title: When you feel flooded
entries.content: In a heated argument the body can 'flood' (heart rate up, hard to listen). An agreed break of 20 to 30 minutes lets the nervous system calm down before talking again.
entries.source: The Gottman Institute; Emotional Flooding - Connected Couples
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: The four warning signs
entries.content: Criticism, contempt, defensiveness and stonewalling strongly predict relationship trouble. Their antidotes: a gentle start, appreciation, taking responsibility, and self-soothing.
entries.source: The Gottman Institute: The Four Horsemen
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Start soft
entries.content: Opening with blame makes people feel attacked and shut down. Describe the situation calmly with an 'I' statement and say what you need: 'I feel hurt when plans change last minute; can we decide by noon?'
entries.source: How To Repair Inevitable Relationship Conflict - Retune Life; Gottman research
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Attachment styles
entries.content: Adult attachment is measured on two scales: anxiety (fear of rejection) and avoidance (discomfort with closeness). Low on both feels 'secure' and handles stress more easily.
entries.source: Attachment theory, individual psychodynamics, and relationship functioning
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Calming anxious attachment
entries.content: If you tend to panic when someone seems distant, pause and check the facts before reacting. Separating what happened from the scary story helps.
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Mindfulness in relationships
entries.content: Attachment anxiety can make it hard to stay present with a partner. Practicing mindfulness together is linked with higher relationship satisfaction.
entries.source: Attachment insecurity and relationship satisfaction - Frontiers
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Appreciation balances criticism
entries.content: Couples who stay happy share far more appreciation than criticism. Name one thing you value about the other person each day.
entries.source: The Gottman Institute: Four Horsemen antidotes
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Family support builds kindness
entries.content: People who grew up with warm, responsive caregivers tend to treat themselves and others more kindly as adults.
entries.source: A meta-analysis of self-compassion and attachment in adults - Cardiff University
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Calm parents, calm kids
entries.content: Parents who feel secure are more attuned to their children's feelings. Consistent comfort teaches kids how to calm their own emotions.
entries.source: Attachment theory, individual psychodynamics, and relationship functioning
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Ask for support
entries.content: When family duties feel heavy, reaching out for emotional support is a strength, not a weakness. Shared stress is lighter stress.
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only
